data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet for the Netherlands summarizes how 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier cycles (notably 2018 and longer trends since 2012). It reports proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2+ and Level 5/6) and mean performance comparisons with the OECD average and selected comparison countries, including uncertainty via confidence intervals. The factsheet also highlights equity-related gaps within the Netherlands (socio-economic status, gender, and immigrant background) and contextual indicators from student, school, and principal questionnaires (e.g., belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences). Methodologically, it emphasizes PISA’s complex sampling and technical standards, noting that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard shortfalls (asterisked), and that higher exclusion rates in the Netherlands in 2022 (often due to disability without adaptation) may bias results upward. No machine-learning models are estimated in this document; it is descriptive reporting from the OECD PISA 2022 Database.
